## What's new in QOTA 16.10.3

- The root `Dockerfile` aligns asset handling with the official Frappe Docker pattern by moving compiled assets from `sites/assets` to `/home/frappe/frappe-bench/assets`, removing `.git` directories from installed apps, dropping image `VOLUME` declarations (leaving `sites` and `logs` persistence to Docker Compose), and setting `/usr/local/bin/main-entrypoint.sh` as `ENTRYPOINT`.
- `main-entrypoint.sh` inspects `sites/assets` at container startup for mountpoints and legacy asset directory safety, refuses destructive changes when an independent mount or unrecognized entry is present, and creates or updates the `sites/assets -> /home/frappe/frappe-bench/assets` symlink.
- `ASSETS_PATH` has been removed from `nginx-entrypoint.sh`, `frappe.conf.template`, and `configure.sh`. Nginx serves `/assets/` directly from `/home/frappe/frappe-bench/assets/` via `alias`, while `configure.sh` verifies the `sites/assets` symlink, validates `assets.json`, `assets-rtl.json`, and their referenced files without copying manifests into the `sites` volume, and invalidates the Redis key `assets_json`.
- Derived images (such as `qota-private`) inherit `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD` unless overridden, can install additional apps across separate `RUN` instructions without `VOLUME` interference, and replace `/home/frappe/frappe-bench/assets` with the newly compiled `sites/assets` after `bench build`.
- Updated `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, and `.dockerignore` with the new entrypoint, Compose volume configuration, upgrade behavior, and derived image pattern.

## Upgrading from 16.10.2

Keep the existing `sites` and `logs` volumes in Docker Compose and remove any `ASSETS_PATH` environment variable from `configurator` and `frontend`. If a separate volume or bind mount is attached to `/home/frappe/frappe-bench/sites/assets`, remove that mount before recreating the containers so `main-entrypoint.sh` can link `sites/assets` to `/home/frappe/frappe-bench/assets`. Legacy `sites/assets` directories inside the `sites` volume containing only recognized Frappe asset entries are replaced automatically at startup. Database upgrades for existing sites remain manual (`bench --site <site> migrate`).
